newsitem.title: USA: Key lawmakers urge Clinton to consider CPI panel.
newsitem.headline: Key lawmakers urge Clinton to consider CPI panel.

text.p: Several key U.S. lawmakers Thursday urged President Clinton to support the creation of an independent panel to make changes to the consumer price index so that it better reflects increases in the cost of living.
Reports that the White House had set aside the idea of forming a bi-partisan commission drew a strong reaction from both Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill.

"I hope the President will reconsider his decision," Delaware Republican William Roth, chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, said at a news conference. "It is important that we are able to precisely measure inflation."

Roth and New York Democrat Patrick Moynihan introduced legislation earlier this week that would create a five-member "cost of living board" that would review government inflation data and produce a cost of living adjustment each year.
A congressionally appointed panel concluded recently that the government's consumer price index overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year.

The group's controversial findings have prompted calls for changes in the way the index is calculated, a move that could lead to cuts in Social Security retirement payments and many other federal benefits that are linked to the CPI.
"Fully one-third of the federal budget is indexed to a formula that is incorrect and inaccurate," said Sen. John Breaux, a Louisiana Democrat.
Breaux called the proposal to create a bi-partisan panel an option that "is politically the most acceptable" and he maintained that there is bi-partisan support for such a plan.

Roth, Moynihan and Breaux were joined at the news conference by the following Senators: Nebraska Democrat Bob Kerrey, North Dakota Democrat Kent Conrad, Virginia Democrat Charles Robb and Rhode Island Republican John Chafee.

House Majority Leader Dick Armey issued a statement saying that the Clinton administration "has a responsibility to be as accurate as possible in the technical analysis it uses to administer the laws of the land."
